question.worked_solution:
The stationary points of a multivariable function $f$ are the points $a$ in the domain of $f$ such that ${f}^{′}(a)={0}^{T},$ where

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]|}_{x=a}.
$$

In tihs case, the domain of $f$ is ${R}^{2},$ and the first partial derivatives of $f$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =4x+4y \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =4x+2y+4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first derivative of $f$ is

$$
{f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}4x+4y & 4x+2y+4\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the stationary points, we need to find the points where ${f}^{′}(x,y)={0}^{T}.$
Setting ${f}^{′}(x,y)={0}^{T},$ we have the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x+4y=0 \\ 4x+2y+4=0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $x$ in the first equation, we get

$$
4x+4y=0\,⟹\,x=-y.
$$

Then, substituting $x=-y$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4(-y)+2y+4 & =0 \\ -4y+2y+4 & =0 \\ -2y & =-4 \\ y & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Back-substituting this value into $x=-y,$ we obtain

$$
y=2\,⟹\,x=-2.
$$

Therefore, our system has one solution, $(-2,2).$

In conclusion, $f$ has one stationary point, $(-2,2).$
